title: 12 Hotel Openings That Could Change Where Conventions Go Through 2030
summary: New headquarters hotels are giving cities the room inventory and meeting space needed to compete for larger conventions. But planners booking years ahead must weigh these opportunities against construction delays and opening-date uncertainty.

title: Where Can Planners Give Attendees Something They Can’t Get Anywhere Else? A Guide to Canada’s Most Distinctive Venues and Experiences
summary: Attendees are asking for an alternative to the traditional meeting environment. In Canada, a collection of venues and team building activities offer planners an opportunity to deliver a different kind of experience.

title: 600 Workers, 14 Venues and a 60-Foot LED Failure: A Look at What Worked and What Didn’t at the B20 Summit
summary: The B20 USA Summit showed how an entire neighborhood can become a conference campus. But the unconventional approach brought infrastructure demands, logistical complications, and security challenges that traditional convention centers are designed to manage.

title: Thoughtful Beats Expensive: An Expert's 10 Rules for Incentive Gifting
summary: With gifting costs up sharply, the most coveted incentive gifts aren't about price or status. They're about the thought behind them.

title: More Than Just a Free Trip: Direct Selling Companies Rethink Their Incentives
summary: Direct selling’s independent reps don’t look like they used to. Neither do the incentive trips designed to reward them.

title: Where Should Associations Draw the Line With Event Outsourcing?
summary: Few associations choose between running everything in-house and handing it all to a professional congress organizer. The harder decisions concern who controls the program, the data, and the attendee relationship, and those deserve more scrutiny than the model itself.

title: The Moscone Leak Closed Microsoft Ignite’s Expo Floor for a Day. Who Pays?
summary: Often, the exhibitors themselves. Venue contracts are written for disasters that cancel an event, not a partial closure like Ignite’s. Planners should know which clauses cover the difference.

title: Why the Human Side of Meetings Matters Even More in the Age of AI
summary: As AI takes on more of the administrative work, planners can spend more time on strategy, creativity, and the human connections that make in-person meetings worth the effort.

title: A Futurist’s Verdict on Meeting Design: Most Stage Time Is Wasted
summary: This keynote speaker asked two questions planners should be asking themselves: Why is most of the expertise at an event sitting in the audience and not being asked to contribute? And why do sponsors still get so much stage time?

title: When Flights Stop, Are Your Meeting Attendees Protected?
summary: Most contracts are written for an event that gets canceled, not one where half the attendees show up a day late. The FAA’s nationwide ground stop exposed a gap in how  planners prepare for travel disruptions.
